_what: Make one pursuit its own Postgres database, closed to every other login, with search by meaning. Input: {operator_credential_name, credential_name, hosts, limits?}: the vault name of the connection of whoever runs the computer (a login with CREATEROLE and CREATEDB: tools/keep-a-postgres-database-on-a-computer set-up-postgres-role.sh PG_MAKES_ROLES=yes PG_MAKES_DATABASES=yes), the vault name the pursuit's own connection is kept under, and the hosts it may go to; limits, when given, are the pursuit login's own connection_limit and statement_timeout_ms, set as the login is made: the numbers the computer's measured capacity allows for one pursuit, never numbers chosen here. First the pursuit's connection is kept: the caller's own computer makes it (postgresql://<role>:<a password made there, never shown>@<the computer's database address>:5432/<database>?sslmode=verify-full, the role and database named for the pursuit; a server reached over the network takes TLS only, and sslrootcert=system breaks node-pg, which reads it as a file name) and pipes it into the vault tool, so no step's input or answer holds it. Then the operator's login runs run-sql-in-my-database's own-database recipe with that connection, which makes the role and the database it owns, closed to everyone else, the operator too, with the limits given; it refuses a pursuit password shorter than 43 characters (32 random bytes as base64url). Then the pursuit's own login turns on pgvector (CREATE EXTENSION vector, an extension its owner may make), and reads back who it is, which database it is in and the vector version. The tables are the pursuit's: its AI makes them in SQL as its lists need them, so nothing here names a list. Used by the saved setup list's keep-data and search-by-meaning choices, once per pursuit. Telling changes is not part of making a database: the person runs workflow:tell-me-when-something-changes when they want their changes told.

definitions.name: Make a pursuit its own database

input.sql: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector
SELECT current_user AS login, current_database() AS database, (SELECT extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'vector') AS vector
